knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Surjectivity Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar differentiable example showing why graphical-derivative coverage must hold uniformly at nearby graph points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[f(0)=0,\qquad f(x)=x+2x^2\sin(x^{-2})\quad(x\ne0).\] Then \(f'(0)=1\), so \(Df(0)(h)=\{h\}\) is surjective. For \(x\ne0\), \[f'(x)=1+4x\sin(x^{-2})-4x^{-1}\cos(x^{-2}),\] and \(f'\) vanishes at a sequence \(x_n\to0\). Consequently no positive graphical-derivative covering rate holds uniformly at nearby graph points, and \(f\) is not metrically regular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Surjectivity of the graphical derivative only at the reference point does not ensure metric regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is defined by the displayed formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise surjectivity of \(Df(0)\) is insufficient for metric regularity at \((0,0)\).

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional normed spaces, \(F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) has locally closed graph, and \((\bar x,\bar y)\in\operatorname{gph}F\).
\(F\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong metric regularity is equivalent to the absence of nonzero horizontal directions in the strict graphical derivative.

notation.meaning: strict graphical derivative formed from nearby graph-point secants
inverse image of the zero direction

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Finite-dimensional strict-derivative injectivity criterion combined with metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional criterion assuming metric regularity separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \((h,k)\in\operatorname{gph}D_*F(\bar x\mid\bar y)\) when there exist distinct nearby graph points \((x_i,y_i),(x_i',y_i')\to(\bar x,\bar y)\) and numbers \(t_i\downarrow0\) such that \[(x_i-x_i')/t_i\to h,\qquad(y_i-y_i')/t_i\to k.\] Under metric regularity, \(F\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) if and only if \[D_*F(\bar x\mid\bar y)^{-1}(0)=\{0\}.\] The strict-derivative condition rules out distinct nearby preimages with vanishing output separation; metric regularity supplies local existence and Lipschitz stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given metric regularity, strong metric regularity is characterized by the strict graphical derivative having no nonzero horizontal direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Graphical-Derivative Criterion for Strong Metric Regularity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Bouligand-Derivative Subregularity Modulus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quantitative form complementing the immutable Bouligand lower-bound equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the uniform expansion \[f(\bar x+h)=f(\bar x)+f'_B(\bar x;h)+o(\|h\|).\] Set \[m_B:=\inf_{\|h\|=1}\|f'_B(\bar x;h)\|.\] Then, with \(1/0=+\infty\), \[\operatorname{subreg}f(\bar x\mid f(\bar x))=m_B^{-1}.\] In particular, strong metric subregularity holds exactly when \(m_B>0\).

assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are finite-dimensional normed spaces and \(f:X\to Y\) has the displayed uniform Bouligand first-order expansion at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Aubin Modulus from the Coderivative Outer Norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative finite-dimensional form of the Mordukhovich criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces and let \(\operatorname{gph}F\) be locally closed at \((\bar x,\bar y)\). If \(F\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar x,\bar y)\), then \[\operatorname{lip}F(\bar x,\bar y)=\lVert D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)\rVert^+:=\sup_{\lVert y^*\rVert\le 1}\sup\{\lVert x^*\rVert:x^*\in D^*F(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\}.\]

children.title: Coderivative-Calculus Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Qualification and compactness boundaries affecting coderivative tests.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact Diagonal Counterexample to the Pointwise Kernel Test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional counterexample showing that a trivial coderivative inverse kernel does not imply metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\ell^2\) and define the bounded linear operator \(T:H\to H\) by \((Tx)_n=x_n/n\). Then \(T=T^*\), \[\ker T^*=\{0\},\qquad (D^*T(0,0))^{-1}(0)=\{0\},\] but \[\inf_{\|y^*\|=1}\|T^*y^*\|=0.\] Consequently, \(T\) has nonclosed range and is not metrically regular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The compact diagonal operator on l2 has an injective adjoint and a trivial pointwise coderivative inverse kernel, yet it is not metrically regular because no uniform adjoint lower bound exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D^*T(0,0))^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\) but \(T\) is not metrically regular at \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Diagonal Counterexample to the Pointwise Kernel Test

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hilbert-Space Closed-Range Boundary for Pointwise Coderivative Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear characterization separating pointwise adjoint injectivity from the uniform lower bound required for metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H_1\to H_2\) be bounded and linear between Hilbert spaces. The following are equivalent: \(T\) is metrically regular; \(T\) is surjective; and there exists \(c>0\) such that \[\|T^*y^*\|\ge c\|y^*\|\qquad(y^*\in H_2).\] Moreover, \[\operatorname{reg}T=\left(\inf_{\|y^*\|=1}\|T^*y^*\|\right)^{-1}.\] The weaker condition \(\ker T^*=\{0\}\) guarantees only that \(\operatorname{rge}T\) is dense and does not imply metric regularity without closed range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For bounded linear Hilbert-space operators, metric regularity requires the adjoint to be uniformly bounded below; adjoint injectivity alone gives only dense range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\text{ is metrically regular}\iff\inf_{\|y^*\|=1}\|T^*y^*\|>0\), whereas \(\ker T^*=\{0\}\) alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Hilbert-Space Closed-Range Boundary for Pointwise Coderivative Tests

assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is the bounded linear map defined by \((Tx)_n=x_n/n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D^*T(0,0))^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), yet \(T\) is not metrically regular at \((0,0)\).

notation.meaning: inverse image of zero under the coderivative multifunction

review_flags: external source desirable for the compactness boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure in infinite dimensions of transferring the finite-dimensional pointwise coderivative test for metric regularity without a uniform estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(T\) is bounded linear and self-adjoint, \(D^*T(0,0)(y^*)=\{T^*y^*\}\). Hence \[(D^*T(0,0))^{-1}(0)=\ker T^*=\{0\}.\] Nevertheless, for the unit vectors \(e_n\), \[\|Te_n\|=\frac{1}{n}\longrightarrow 0.\] Thus \(T\) is not bounded below, its range is not closed, and it is not metrically regular at \((0,0)\). The finite-dimensional pointwise coderivative criterion therefore cannot be transferred unchanged without an appropriate compactness hypothesis or uniform neighborhood estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The injective adjoint of a compact diagonal operator has a trivial coderivative inverse kernel, but the operator is not metrically regular, exposing the infinite-dimensional compactness boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: BIF condition for a parametric variational inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local implicit-solution assumption at a feasible parameter-solution pair; uniqueness is restricted to the stated solution neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\bar x,\bar y)\in\mathcal F$. The BIF condition holds if there exist an open neighborhood $U\times V$ of $(\bar x,\bar y)$ and a Lipschitz map $y:U\cap X\to V$ such that $y(\bar x)=\bar y$, $y$ is directionally differentiable (hence B-differentiable) at $\bar x$, and, for every $x\in U\cap X$, $y(x)$ is the unique solution in $V$ of $\operatorname{VI}(F(x,\cdot),C(x))$. Solutions outside $V$ need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible pair, BIF requires a local Lipschitz implicit solution function that is directionally differentiable at the reference parameter and gives the unique variational-inequality solution near the reference solution for every nearby admissible parameter. Other solutions may exist outside that neighborhood.

Then, after shrinking neighborhoods if necessary, \[S(p_1)\cap U\,\subset\,S(p_2)+\kappa\lambda d(p_1,p_2)\mathbb B_X.\] Hence the implicit solution map \(S\) has the Aubin property around \((\bar p,\bar x)\).

children.title: Calmness Criteria for Implicit Solution Maps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Calmness Does Not Imply the Aubin Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-valued implicit solution map separating reference-centered calmness from pairwise Lipschitz-like behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) by \(g(0)=0\) and \(g(p)=p\sin(1/p)\) for \(p\ne0\), let \(F(p,x):=x-g(p)\), and let \(S(p):=\{x:0=F(p,x)\}=\{g(p)\}\). Then \[|g(p)-g(0)|\le |p|,\] so \(S\) is calm at \((0,0)\). However, \(g\) is not locally Lipschitz on any neighborhood of \(0\), and therefore \(S\) lacks the Aubin property around \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The implicit branch p sin(1/p) is calm at the origin but is not Lipschitz-like there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is calm at \((0,0)\) but lacks the Aubin property around \((0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Calmness Does Not Imply the Aubin Property

assumptions_latex: The reference generalized equation satisfies a local error bound with constant \(\kappa\).
Nearby parameter solutions generate residuals for the reference equation bounded by \(\lambda d(p,\bar p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is calm at \((\bar p,\bar x)\), with calmness modulus at most \(\kappa\lambda\).
review_flags: exact residual-transfer assumptions require a theorem-level source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference-parameter error-bound criterion for calmness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose locally \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S(\bar p))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,F(\bar p,x)),\] and every nearby \(x\in S(p)\) satisfies \[\operatorname{dist}(0,F(\bar p,x))\leq\lambda d(p,\bar p).\] Then \[S(p)\cap U\subset S(\bar p)+\kappa\lambda d(p,\bar p)\mathbb B_X.\] Therefore \(S\) is calm at \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Unlike the Aubin property, this estimate compares all nearby parameters only with the fixed reference parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reference-equation error bound and controlled parameter residuals imply calmness of the implicit solution map.

children.title: Isolated-Calmness Criteria

knowledge_statements.title: Isolated-Calmness Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional graphical-derivative characterization of isolated calmness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P,X,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces, let \(F:P\times X\rightrightarrows Y\), and define \(S:P\rightrightarrows X\) by \(S(p):=\{x\in X\mid 0\in F(p,x)\}\). Isolated calmness of \(S\) at \((\bar p,\bar x)\in\operatorname{gph}S\) means that there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\), and \(\kappa\geq0\), such that \[S(p)\cap V\subset \bar x+\kappa\lVert p-\bar p\rVert\mathbb B\qquad(p\in U).\] If \(\operatorname{gph}S\) is locally closed at \((\bar p,\bar x)\), this property is equivalent to \[DS(\bar p,\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional solution map with locally closed graph, isolated calmness is equivalent to its graphical derivative having no nonzero solution displacement in the zero parameter direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Implicit-Function Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-metric-regularity form of the parametric implicit-function theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P,X,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces and define \(S(p):=\{x\in X\mid0\in f(p,x)+Q(x)\}\). Suppose \(f\) is locally Lipschitz in \(p\), uniformly for \(x\) near \(\bar x\), is continuously differentiable in \(x\) near \((\bar p,\bar x)\), and the frozen mapping \(x\mapsto f(\bar p,x)+Q(x)\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\). Then there are neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\) and \(V\) of \(\bar x\), and a single-valued Lipschitz map \(s:U\to V\), such that \[S(p)\cap V=\{s(p)\},\qquad s(\bar p)=\bar x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong metric regularity of the frozen generalized equation, together with a locally uniform Lipschitz parameter perturbation, yields a unique local solution branch that is Lipschitz in the parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(P,X,Y\) are finite-dimensional normed spaces, \(f:P\times X\to Y\), and \(Q:X\rightrightarrows Y\).
\(f\) is locally Lipschitz in \(p\), uniformly for \(x\) near \(\bar x\), and continuously differentiable in \(x\) near \((\bar p,\bar x)\).
\(Q\) has locally closed graph and \(0\in f(\bar p,\bar x)+Q(\bar x)\).
\(x\mapsto f(\bar p,x)+Q(x)\) is strongly metrically regular at \((\bar x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local solution map \(S(p):=\{x\in X\mid0\in f(p,x)+Q(x)\}\) admits a unique Lipschitz localization near \((\bar p,\bar x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong Monotonicity Controls the Inverse Only on the Range
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates inverse uniqueness and slope control from surjectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone, then \(A^{-1}\) is single-valued on \(\operatorname{rge}A\) and satisfies \[\|A^{-1}(y_1)-A^{-1}(y_2)\|\leq \mu^{-1}\|y_1-y_2\|\qquad(y_1,y_2\in\operatorname{rge}A).\] Strong monotonicity alone does not imply \(\operatorname{rge}A=H\): the mapping \(A(x)=x\) with domain \((0,\infty)\subset\mathbb R\) is strongly monotone but has range \((0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity gives uniqueness and reciprocal-modulus stability on the operator range, while maximality or another existence hypothesis is needed for an everywhere-defined inverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{-1}\) is single-valued and \(1/\mu\)-Lipschitz on \(\operatorname{rge}A\), but need not be defined on all of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Monotonicity Controls the Inverse Only on the Range

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly Monotone Variational-Inequality Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space variational inequality over a nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(C\subset H\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:H\to H\) be continuous and \(\mu\)-strongly monotone for some \(\mu>0\). Then \(A:=f+N_C\) is maximal and \(\mu\)-strongly monotone. Consequently, for every \(y\in H\), the inclusion \[y\in f(x)+N_C(x)\] has exactly one solution \(x=s(y)\), and \[\|s(y_1)-s(y_2)\|\leq \mu^{-1}\|y_1-y_2\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous strongly monotone variational inequality over a closed convex set has a globally unique solution for every right-hand side, with reciprocal-modulus Lipschitz stability.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f:H\to H\) is continuous and \(\mu\)-strongly monotone for some \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((f+N_C)^{-1}:H\to H\) is single-valued and \(1/\mu\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Monotone Variational-Inequality Criterion

assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space \(H\).
For some \(\mu>0\), \(\langle y_1-y_2,x_1-x_2\rangle\geq\mu\lVert x_1-x_2\rVert^2\) whenever \(y_i\in A(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{-1}:H\to H\) is single-valued and \(1/\mu\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space criterion based on maximal strong monotonicity.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Set-Valued Mappings p. 148

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal and \(\mu\)-strongly monotone. Then every \(y\in H\) has a unique solution \(x=A^{-1}(y)\). Moreover, for \(x_i=A^{-1}(y_i)\), strong monotonicity and Cauchy--Schwarz give the stability estimate \[\lVert x_1-x_2\rVert\leq\mu^{-1}\lVert y_1-y_2\rVert.\] Hence the generalized equation \(y\in A(x)\) has a globally single-valued Lipschitz solution mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal strongly monotone operator has an everywhere-defined, single-valued inverse whose Lipschitz modulus is at most the reciprocal strong-monotonicity modulus.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Mapping Criteria

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotics and Realization of Lipschitz-Stable Near-Optimal Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak and strong normalized-displacement limits and realizable second-order paths under an exact second-order value formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $X$ be reflexive. Suppose that $\Lambda(x_0,u_0)\neq\varnothing$, directional regularity holds,
$$\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(u(t))-v(u_0)-t\operatorname{val}(PL_d)}{\tfrac12t^2}=\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ}^R),$$
and $D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(\cdot,\cdot)$ is weakly lower semicontinuous for every $\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0,u_0)$. Then: (a) if $\bar x(t)$ is a Lipschitz-stable $o(t^2)$-optimal solution, every weak limit point of $t^{-1}(\bar x(t)-x_0)$ belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathcal{DQ}^R)$; (b) if additionally $D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(\cdot,\cdot)$ is a Legendre form for every $\lambda\in\mathcal S(DL_d)$, every such weak limit point is also a strong limit point, and if $\mathcal{DQ}^R$ has the unique solution $\bar h$, then
$$\bar x(t)=x_0+t\bar h+o(t);$$
(c) for every $h\in\mathcal S(\mathcal{DQ}^R)$ and $w\in\mathcal S(PQ_h)$, there exists an $o(t^2)$-optimal solution path
$$x(t)=x_0+th+\tfrac12t^2w+o(t^2).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an exact second-order value formula, directional regularity, nonempty multipliers, and weak lower semicontinuity, weak normalized-displacement limits of a Lipschitz-stable near-optimal path solve the relaxed directional quadratic problem. Legendre Hessian forms upgrade these limits to strong ones, uniqueness gives a first-order expansion, and compatible first- and second-order model solutions can be realized by a near-optimal path.
assumptions_latex: D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(\cdot,\cdot)\text{ is weakly lower semicontinuous for every }\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0,u_0)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every weak limit point of }t^{-1}(\bar x(t)-x_0)\text{ lies in }\mathcal S(\mathcal{DQ}^R);\quad \mathcal S(\mathcal{DQ}^R)=\{\bar h\}\Rightarrow\bar x(t)=x_0+t\bar h+o(t);\quad \forall h\in\mathcal S(\mathcal{DQ}^R),\ w\in\mathcal S(PQ_h),\ \exists x(t)=x_0+th+\tfrac12t^2w+o(t^2)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semistable, stable, and strongly stable VI solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Lipschitz-type stability of a fixed-set variational inequality under perturbations of its mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F). It is semistable if, for every open neighborhood \mathcal N of x^* satisfying the standing localization condition (5.1.1), there exist c,\varepsilon>0 such that every G\in\mathbb B(F;\varepsilon,K_{\mathcal N}) and every x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,G)\cap\mathcal N satisfy \|x-x^*\|\le c\|F(x)-G(x)\|. It is stable if, additionally, \operatorname{SOL}(K,G)\cap\mathcal N\ne\varnothing for every such G. It is strongly stable if it is stable and, for the same local constants, any continuous G,\widetilde G\in\mathbb B(F;\varepsilon,K_{\mathcal N}) and any x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,G)\cap\mathcal N,\ x'\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,\widetilde G)\cap\mathcal N satisfy \|x-x'\|\le c\|(F(x)-G(x))-(F(x')-\widetilde G(x'))\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A VI solution is semistable when every sufficiently small local perturbation of the mapping obeys a uniform error-to-solution-distance bound. Stability additionally requires a nearby perturbed solution to exist. Strong stability additionally bounds the distance between solutions of any two nearby continuous perturbations by the difference of their perturbation errors.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal N\text{ is an open neighborhood of }x^*\text{ satisfying (5.1.1)}
G,\widetilde G\in\mathbb B(F;\varepsilon,K_{\mathcal N})\text{ are continuous in the strong-stability clause}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed local error bounds and, for stability, local existence define semistability, stability, and strong stability.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates strong stability with a Schur-complement P-matrix condition and a common-sign determinant condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be continuously differentiable near a solution \(x^*\) of \(\operatorname{NCP}(F)\), with support set \(\gamma\) and degenerate set \(\beta\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(x^*\) is strongly stable; (ii) \(J_\gamma F_\gamma(x^*)\) is nonsingular and
\[J_\beta F_\beta(x^*)-J_\gamma F_\beta(x^*)[J_\gamma F_\gamma(x^*)]^{-1}J_\beta F_\gamma(x^*)\]
is a \(P\)-matrix; (iii) there exists \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\) such that, for every \(\gamma'\) satisfying \(\gamma\subseteq\gamma'\subseteq\gamma\cup\beta\),
\[\det JF(x)_{\gamma'\gamma'}=\sigma.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong stability and b-regularity of NCP solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates strong stability, strong b-regularity, and b-regularity while preserving the additional P0 hypothesis required for the latter equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near a solution \(x^*\) of \(\operatorname{NCP}(F)\). Then \(x^*\) is strongly stable if and only if it is strongly b-regular. If \(JF(x^*)_{\bar\alpha\bar\alpha}\) is a \(P_0\)-matrix, then strong stability, strong b-regularity, and b-regularity of \(x^*\) are equivalent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A parameterized homogeneous MLCP sufficient condition for NCP stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a sufficient stability condition in terms of unique zero solvability of a family of homogeneous MLCPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near a solution \(x^*\) of \(\operatorname{NCP}(F)\), and let \(\gamma\) and \(\beta\) be respectively the support and degenerate index sets of \(x^*\). If, for every \(\tau\geq0\), the homogeneous MLCP
\[0=(\tau I_{|\gamma|}+J_\gamma F_\gamma(x^*))d x_\gamma+J_\beta F_\gamma(x^*)d x_\beta,\]
\[0\leq J_\gamma F_\beta(x^*)d x_\gamma+(\tau I_{|\beta|}+J_\beta F_\beta(x^*))d x_\beta\ \perp\ d x_\beta\geq0\]
has the unique solution \((d x_\gamma,d x_\beta)=(0,0)\), then \(x^*\) is a stable solution of \(\operatorname{NCP}(F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An NCP solution is stable if every nonnegative diagonal shift of its support-degenerate homogeneous MLCP has only the zero solution.
assumptions_latex: \gamma\text{ and }\beta\text{ are the support and degenerate sets of }x^*
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is a stable solution of }\operatorname{NCP}(F)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order sensitivity under regularity of the outer function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional composite parametric optimization along a directional perturbation path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(X\) is finite dimensional, \(\mathcal S(u_0)=\{x_0\}\), \(\Lambda(x_0,u_0)\neq\varnothing\), the directional regularity condition holds, there exists an \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution of \((P_{u(t)})\) that is Lipschitz stable at \(x_0\), and \(g\) is second-order regular at \(y_0=F(x_0,u_0)\). Then, as \(t\downarrow0\), \[v(u(t))=v(u_0)+t\operatorname{val}(PL_d)+\tfrac12t^2\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ})+o(t^2).\] For any \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution \(\bar x(t)\), every accumulation point of \((\bar x(t)-x_0)/t\) solves \(\mathcal{DQ}\). If \(\mathcal{DQ}\) has the unique solution \(\widehat h\), every Lipschitz-stable \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution satisfies \(\bar x(t)=x_0+t\widehat h+o(t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated finite-dimensional composite problem, uniqueness and multiplier existence, directional regularity, a Lipschitz-stable near-optimal solution, and second-order regularity of the outer function yield a second-order value expansion. Scaled accumulation points of near-optimal solutions solve the directional quadratic problem, and uniqueness of its solution determines the first-order expansion of Lipschitz-stable near-optimal solutions.
assumptions_latex: There exists an \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution of \((P_{u(t)})\) that is Lipschitz stable at \(x_0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated second-order value expansion holds; every accumulation point of the scaled displacement of an \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution solves \(\mathcal{DQ}\), and uniqueness of its optimizer \(\widehat h\) implies \(\bar x(t)=x_0+t\widehat h+o(t)\) for Lipschitz-stable \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded proximal subgradients characterize local Lipschitz continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional criterion for a lower-semicontinuous extended-real function at a point of its domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be lower semicontinuous, let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), and let \(K>0\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(f\) is Lipschitz continuous with Lipschitz constant \(K\) on some neighborhood of \(\bar x\); (ii) there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \(y\in\mathbb{R}^k\) and \(\xi\in\partial^P f(y)\), \(\|y-\bar x\|\leq\varepsilon\) and \(|f(y)-f(\bar x)|\leq\varepsilon\) imply \(\|\xi\|\leq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower-semicontinuous extended-real function is locally Lipschitz with constant K near a domain point exactly when all proximal subgradients at nearby graph points have norm at most K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[f\text{ is locally }K\text{-Lipschitz near }\bar x\bigr]\iff\bigl[\exists\varepsilon>0\;\forall y,\xi\in\partial^P f(y): (\|y-\bar x\|\leq\varepsilon\land |f(y)-f(\bar x)|\leq\varepsilon)\Rightarrow\|\xi\|\leq K\bigr]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Multiplier Variation Estimate at a Nondegenerate Solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds multiplier variation between nearby parameter-solution pairs; it does not by itself establish Lipschitz dependence of multipliers on the parameter alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong stability, strong regularity, and local Lipschitz invertibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability properties of a zero of a continuous finite-dimensional equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, where \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open, and let \(x\in\mathcal D\) satisfy \(H(x)=0\). Then: (a) \(x\) is strongly stable if and only if \(x\) is strongly regular; (b) if \(H\) is a locally Lipschitz homeomorphism at \(x\), then \(x\) is strongly stable; and (c) if \(H\) is locally Lipschitz continuous at \(x\) and \(x\) is strongly stable, then \(H\) is a locally Lipschitz homeomorphism at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a zero of a continuous finite-dimensional equation, strong stability is equivalent to strong regularity. Local Lipschitz invertibility implies strong stability, and the converse holds when the map is locally Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is strongly stable}\iff x\text{ is strongly regular};\quad H\text{ locally Lipschitz homeomorphic at }x\Rightarrow x\text{ strongly stable};\quad [H\text{ locally Lipschitz at }x\land x\text{ strongly stable}]\Rightarrow H\text{ locally Lipschitz homeomorphic at }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local perturbation stability of a nondegenerate complementarity solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistence, local uniqueness, and a quantitative bound for perturbed complementarity solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F,G:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable on an open set \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let \(x^*\) be a nondegenerate solution of \(\operatorname{CP}(F,G)\). Suppose the \(n\times n\) matrix with rows \(\nabla F_i(x^*)^T\) for \(i\in\alpha_F\) and \(\nabla G_i(x^*)^T\) for \(i\in\alpha_G\) is nonsingular. For every open neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x^*\) such that \(x^*\) is the unique solution of \(\operatorname{CP}(F,G)\) in \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\), there exist \(\varepsilon,c>0\) such that, for any continuous pairs \((F^i,G^i)\), \(i=1,2\), satisfying \(\sup_{z\in\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N}\max\{\|F(z)-F^i(z)\|,\|G(z)-G^i(z)\|\}<\varepsilon\), each \(\operatorname{CP}(F^i,G^i)\) has a unique solution \(x^i\in\mathcal N\), and \(\|x^1-x^2\|\le c\max\{\|F(x^1)-F(x^2)\|,\|G(x^1)-G(x^2)\|\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under nondegeneracy and the stated active-gradient nonsingularity condition, an isolated complementarity solution persists uniquely under sufficiently small uniform perturbations, and the two perturbed solutions obey the stated quantitative bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open and \(F,G:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\) are continuously differentiable.
\(\mathcal N\) is open and \(x^*\) is the unique solution of \(\operatorname{CP}(F,G)\) in \(\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\varepsilon,c>0\ \forall i\in\{1,2\}:\left[\sup_{z\in\operatorname{cl}\mathcal N}\max\{\|F(z)-F^i(z)\|,\|G(z)-G^i(z)\|\}<\varepsilon\right]\Rightarrow\left[\operatorname{CP}(F^i,G^i)\text{ has a unique }x^i\in\mathcal N\right],\quad \|x^1-x^2\|\le c\max\{\|F(x^1)-F(x^2)\|,\|G(x^1)-G(x^2)\|\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Natural-residual error-bound characterization of VI semistability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of strong stability for a polyhedral VI
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equates strong stability with global properties of the critical-cone normal map and unique solvability of associated affine variational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a polyhedron, let \(\mathcal D\) be an open set containing \(K\), and let \(F:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\). Suppose \(x^*\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\) and \(F\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^*\). Set \(\mathcal C=\mathcal C(x^*;K,F)\), and let \(J\mathbf F_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{nor}}\) be the normal map of \((\mathcal C,JF(x^*))\). The following are equivalent: (a) \(x^*\) is strongly stable; (b) \(J\mathbf F_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{nor}}\) is a Lipschitz homeomorphism on \(\mathbb R^n\); (c) it is coherently oriented; (d) it is open; (e) for every \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\operatorname{AVI}(\mathcal C,q,JF(x^*))\) has a unique solution; and (f) \(0\) is strongly stable for \(\operatorname{AVI}(\mathcal C,0,JF(x^*))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth VI over a polyhedron, strong stability is equivalent to the critical-cone normal map being a Lipschitz homeomorphism, coherently oriented, or open; equivalently, every associated affine VI is uniquely solvable, or zero is strongly stable for the homogeneous affine VI.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open and }K\subseteq\mathcal D
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(a)}\iff\text{(b)}\iff\text{(c)}\iff\text{(d)}\iff\text{(e)}\iff\text{(f)}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min-Max Lower Bound for Second-Order Value Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional lower bound obtained from upper second-order approximation sets of the constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume: (i) $X$ is finite dimensional; (ii) $\mathcal S(u_0)=\{x_0\}$ and $\Lambda(x_0,u_0)\neq\varnothing$; (iii) directional regularity holds in direction $d$; (iv) $(P_{u(t)})$ has an $o(t^2)$-optimal solution $\bar x(t)$ that is Lipschitz stable at $x_0$; and (v) for every $h\in\mathcal S(PL_d)$ there is an upper second-order approximation set $\mathcal A(h,d)$ of $K$ at $y_0:=G(x_0,u_0)$ in direction $DG(x_0,u_0)(h,d)$ relative to $M:=D_xG(x_0,u_0)$. Then $$\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(u(t))-v(u_0)-t\operatorname{val}(PL_d)}{\tfrac12t^2}\geq\vartheta(d,r),$$ where $$\vartheta(d,r):=\min_{h\in\mathcal S(PL_d)}\max_{\lambda\in\mathcal S(DL_d)}\theta_h(\lambda),$$ and $$\theta_h(\lambda):=D_uL(x_0,\lambda,u_0)r+D^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)((h,d),(h,d))-\sigma(\lambda,\mathcal A(h,d)).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In finite dimensions, uniqueness of the reference solution, nonempty multipliers, directional regularity, a Lipschitz-stable near-optimal path, and suitable upper second-order constraint approximations give a lower bound on the second-order directional growth of the value function. The bound is the value of a min-max problem over first-order primal solutions and directional dual solutions.
assumptions_latex: \forall h\in\mathcal S(PL_d),\ \mathcal A(h,d)\text{ is an upper second-order approximation set of }K\text{ at }y_0\text{ in direction }DG(x_0,u_0)(h,d)\text{ relative to }D_xG(x_0,u_0)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stability, derivative-zero, and R0 implications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Links stability of a fixed-set VI solution to normal-map derivative isolation and critical-cone R0 conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that CRCQ holds at \(x^*\) or \(\mathcal M^e(x^*)\) is a singleton. Then \((a)\Rightarrow(b)\Leftrightarrow(c)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under CRCQ or uniqueness of the extreme multiplier pair, stability implies that the normal-map derivative has only the zero direction as a zero, and this derivative condition is equivalent to the R0 property for every extreme-multiplier critical-cone pair.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order value and solution expansion under directional regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional parametric optimization along the perturbation path \(u(t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(X\) is finite dimensional, \(\mathcal S(u_0)=\{x_0\}\), \(\Lambda(x_0,u_0)\neq\varnothing\), directional regularity holds in direction \(d\), and there exists an \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution of \((P_{u(t)})\) that is Lipschitz stable at \(x_0\). Suppose also that, for every \(h\in\mathcal S(PL_d)\), \(K\) is second-order regular at \(G(x_0,u_0)\) in direction \(DG(x_0,u_0)(h,d)\) with respect to \(D_xG(x_0,u_0)\). Then \(\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ})\) is finite and, as \(t\downarrow0\), \[v(u(t))=v(u_0)+t\operatorname{val}(PL_d)+\tfrac12t^2\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ})+o(t^2).\] For any \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution \(\bar x(t)\), every accumulation point of \((\bar x(t)-x_0)/t\) solves \(\mathcal{DQ}\). If \(\bar h\) solves \(\mathcal{DQ}\) and a corresponding solution \(\bar w\) of \(PQ_{\bar h}\) exists, there is an \(o(t^2)\)-optimal path \(\widehat x(t)=x_0+t\bar h+\tfrac12t^2\bar w+o(t^2)\). If \(\mathcal{DQ}\) has the unique solution \(\widehat h\), every Lipschitz-stable \(o(t^2)\)-optimal path satisfies \(\bar x(t)=x_0+t\widehat h+o(t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated finite-dimensional uniqueness, multiplier, directional-regularity, Lipschitz-stability, and second-order-regularity assumptions, the directional quadratic problem has finite value and determines the second-order value expansion and first-order limits of near-optimal solutions. Compatible directional solutions generate second-order near-optimal paths, while uniqueness gives a unique first-order solution expansion.
assumptions_latex: There exists an \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution of \((P_{u(t)})\) that is Lipschitz stable at \(x_0\)
For every \(h\in\mathcal S(PL_d)\), \(K\) has the stated second-order regularity with respect to \(D_xG(x_0,u_0)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ})\in\mathbb R\); the stated value expansion and accumulation-point characterization hold. When the required directional optimizers exist they generate a second-order near-optimal path, and uniqueness of the \(\mathcal{DQ}\) optimizer implies \(\bar x(t)=x_0+t\widehat h+o(t)\) for Lipschitz-stable near-optimal paths.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz sensitivity of P-matrix LCP solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: P-matrix specialization of solution-map Lipschitz stability: global dependence on the right-hand side for a fixed matrix and local joint dependence on the right-hand side and matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\cap\mathbf P. For q,q'\in\mathbb R^n, let z^* and z' be the unique solutions of \operatorname{LCP}(q,M) and \operatorname{LCP}(q',M), respectively. Then \|z^*-z'\|_\infty\le c(M)^{-1}\|q-q'\|_\infty. Moreover, for each q\in\mathbb R^n, there exist a neighborhood U of (q,M) and c'>0 such that, if (q^i,M^i)\in U and M^i\in\mathbf P for i=1,2, then the corresponding unique solutions satisfy \|z^1-z^2\|_\infty\le c'\bigl(\|q^1-q^2\|_\infty+\|M^1-M^2\|_\infty\bigr).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a P-matrix LCP, the unique solution is globally Lipschitz in the right-hand side when the matrix is fixed and locally Lipschitz under simultaneous perturbations of the right-hand side and P-matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|z^*-z'\|_\infty\le c(M)^{-1}\|q-q'\|_\infty,\qquad \|z^1-z^2\|_\infty\le c'\bigl(\|q^1-q^2\|_\infty+\|M^1-M^2\|_\infty\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strong stability equivalence for a VI solution and its normal-map zero

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonzero proximal subgradients of an upper truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-subdifferential rule for truncating a lower-semicontinuous extended-real function from above.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^k\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be lower semicontinuous, let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^k\), let \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}\), and define \(g(y):=\min\{f(y),\beta\}\). If \(0\neq\xi\in\partial^P g(x)\), then \(f(x)\leq\beta\) and \(\xi\in\partial^P f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any nonzero proximal subgradient of a function truncated from above occurs where the original function does not exceed the truncation level, and it is also a proximal subgradient of the original function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x)\leq\beta\quad\text{and}\quad\xi\in\partial^P f(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order Hadamard value differentiability from directional sufficient conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional parametric optimization under directional second-order sufficient conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(X\) is finite dimensional, \(x_0\) is the unique optimal solution of \((P_{u_0})\), directional regularity holds in direction \(d\), and the directional second-order sufficient conditions hold at \(x_0\). Suppose that, for every path \(\widehat u_t=u_0+td+\tfrac12t^2r+o(t^2)\), an \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution path of \((P_{\widehat u_t})\) exists for all sufficiently small \(t>0\) and converges to \(x_0\). Then \(v\) is second-order Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(u_0\) in direction \(d\), with \[v'(u_0;d)=\operatorname{val}(PL_d),\qquad v''(u_0;d,r)=\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ}).\] In addition, every \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution \(\bar x(t)\) of \((P_{u(t)})\) is Lipschitz stable at \(x_0\), and every accumulation point of \((\bar x(t)-x_0)/t\) as \(t\downarrow0\) solves \(\mathcal{DQ}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniqueness, directional regularity, directional second-order sufficiency, and the existence of convergent near-optimal solutions along every second-order perturbation path imply second-order Hadamard directional differentiability of the value function. Its derivatives are the values of the linearized and directional quadratic problems; near-optimal solutions are Lipschitz stable and their scaled accumulation points solve the directional quadratic problem.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0\) is the unique optimal solution of \((P_{u_0})\)
The directional second-order sufficient conditions hold at \(x_0\)
For every \(\widehat u_t=u_0+td+\tfrac12t^2r+o(t^2)\), a convergent \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution path exists for all sufficiently small \(t>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v'(u_0;d)=\operatorname{val}(PL_d)\) and \(v''(u_0;d,r)=\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ})\); every \(o(t^2)\)-optimal solution of \((P_{u(t)})\) is Lipschitz stable at \(x_0\), and every accumulation point of its scaled displacement solves \(\mathcal{DQ}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: NCP stability characterized by a homogeneous MLCP under a P0 condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes stability using unique zero solvability of the unshifted support-degenerate MLCP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuously differentiable near a solution \(x^*\) of \(\operatorname{NCP}(F)\), with support set \(\gamma\) and degenerate set \(\beta\). If
\[\begin{bmatrix}J_\gamma F_\gamma(x^*)&J_\beta F_\gamma(x^*)\\J_\gamma F_\beta(x^*)&J_\beta F_\beta(x^*)\end{bmatrix}\]
is a \(P_0\)-matrix, then \(x^*\) is stable if and only if the homogeneous MLCP
\[0=J_\gamma F_\gamma(x^*)d x_\gamma+J_\beta F_\gamma(x^*)d x_\beta,\]
\[0\leq J_\gamma F_\beta(x^*)d x_\gamma+J_\beta F_\beta(x^*)d x_\beta\ \perp\ d x_\beta\geq0\]
has \((d x_\gamma,d x_\beta)=(0,0)\) as its unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated P0 condition on the support-degenerate Jacobian block, an NCP solution is stable exactly when its homogeneous MLCP has only the zero solution.
assumptions_latex: \gamma\text{ and }\beta\text{ are the support and degenerate sets of }x^*
\begin{bmatrix}J_\gamma F_\gamma(x^*)&J_\beta F_\gamma(x^*)\\J_\gamma F_\beta(x^*)&J_\beta F_\beta(x^*)\end{bmatrix}\text{ is a }P_0\text{-matrix}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ is stable}\iff\operatorname{SOL}(\operatorname{MLCP}_0)=\{(0,0)\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solution-distance bound under objective and feasible-set perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quadratic-growth estimate incorporating objective variation, directed feasible-set deviations, and optimization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_0\) be the optimal-solution set of the unperturbed problem and let \(N\) be a neighborhood of \(S_0\). Suppose the second-order growth condition with constant \(c>0\) holds on \(N\), \(f\) and \(g\) are Lipschitz continuous on \(N\) with moduli \(\eta_1\) and \(\eta_2\), and \(g-f\) is Lipschitz continuous on \(N\) with modulus \(\kappa\). Define \[\delta_1:=\sup_{x\in\Omega\cap N}\operatorname{dist}(x,\Phi\cap N),\qquad \delta_2:=\sup_{x_0\in S_0}\operatorname{dist}(x_0,\Omega\cap N).\] Then every \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution \(\bar x\in N\) of the perturbed problem satisfies \[\operatorname{dist}(\bar x,S_0)\le c^{-1}\kappa+2\delta_1+c^{-1/2}(\eta_1\delta_1+\eta_2\delta_2)^{1/2}+c^{-1/2}\varepsilon^{1/2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under quadratic growth and Lipschitz objective data, the distance from a perturbed epsilon-optimal solution to the original solution set is controlled by objective variation, two directed feasible-set deviations, and square-root optimization error.
assumptions_latex: S_0\text{ is the unperturbed optimal-solution set}
c>0\text{ is the second-order growth constant on }N
f\text{ and }g\text{ are Lipschitz continuous on }N\text{ with moduli }\eta_1,\eta_2
g-f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous on }N\text{ with modulus }\kappa
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}(\bar x,S_0)\le c^{-1}\kappa+2\delta_1+c^{-1/2}(\eta_1\delta_1+\eta_2\delta_2)^{1/2}+c^{-1/2}\varepsilon^{1/2}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-Branch Stability Implies Aubin Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local implication from a unique Lipschitz localization to set-valued Lipschitz stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar p\), \(V\) of \(\bar x\), and an \(L\)-Lipschitz mapping \(s:U\to V\) satisfy \(S(p)\cap V=\{s(p)\}\) for every \(p\in U\). After shrinking the neighborhoods if necessary,
\[
S(p_1)\cap V\subset S(p_2)+L\lVert p_1-p_2\rVert\mathbb B
\quad(p_1,p_2\in U).
\]
Thus the localization has the Aubin property with modulus at most \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unique Lipschitz solution branch automatically gives localized set-valued Lipschitz stability with no larger modulus.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{lip}S(\bar p,\bar x)\le L\) for the localized solution map.
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Branch Stability Implies Aubin Stability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local, locally Lipschitz, and globally Lipschitz homeomorphisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three nested regularity notions for maps from open subsets of Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n be open and \Phi:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n. The map \Phi is a local homeomorphism at x\in\mathcal D if some open neighborhood \mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal D of x makes \Phi|_{\mathcal N}:\mathcal N\to\Phi(\mathcal N) a homeomorphism; its inverse is a local inverse of \Phi. It is a locally Lipschitz homeomorphism at x if such an \mathcal N exists and both \Phi|_{\mathcal N} and (\Phi|_{\mathcal N})^{-1} are Lipschitz on their respective domains. It is a globally Lipschitz homeomorphism if \mathcal D=\mathbb R^n, \Phi is a homeomorphism of \mathbb R^n onto itself, and both \Phi and \Phi^{-1} are globally Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local homeomorphism is homeomorphic on a neighborhood of the point. It is locally Lipschitz when the restricted map and its local inverse are Lipschitz. It is globally Lipschitz when it is a global self-homeomorphism of Euclidean space and both directions are globally Lipschitz.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathcal D\text{ for the local notions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{local homeomorphism at }x\iff\exists\mathcal N\ni x:\Phi|_{\mathcal N}\text{ is a homeomorphism onto }\Phi(\mathcal N);\\&\text{locally Lipschitz homeomorphism at }x\iff\text{the restriction and its inverse are Lipschitz};\\&\text{globally Lipschitz homeomorphism}\iff\mathcal D=\mathbb R^n,\ \Phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\text{ is a homeomorphism, and }\Phi,\Phi^{-1}\text{ are globally Lipschitz}.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Lipschitz Continuity and Local Upper Lipschitz Continuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines two pointwise regularity notions for a single-valued mapping; the second compares values only with the value at the reference point and is therefore weaker than local Lipschitz continuity on a neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping $z:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}^q$ is locally Lipschitz continuous at $x^0\in\mathbb{R}^p$ if there exist an open neighborhood $V_\varepsilon(x^0)$ and a constant $l<\infty$ such that $\|z(x)-z(x')\|\le l\|x-x'\|$ for all $x,x'\in V_\varepsilon(x^0)$. It is locally upper Lipschitz continuous at $x^0$ if there exist an open neighborhood $V_\varepsilon(x^0)$ and a constant $l<\infty$ such that $\|z(x)-z(x^0)\|\le l\|x-x^0\|$ for all $x\in V_\varepsilon(x^0)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map is locally Lipschitz at a reference point when one finite Lipschitz constant bounds the change between every pair of points in some neighborhood. It is locally upper Lipschitz there when such a bound is required only between each nearby point and the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,V_\varepsilon(x^0)\text{ open},\ l<\infty:\ \forall x,x'\in V_\varepsilon(x^0),\ \|z(x)-z(x')\|\le l\|x-x'\|;\quad\text{or, for local upper Lipschitz continuity, }\forall x\in V_\varepsilon(x^0),\ \|z(x)-z(x^0)\|\le l\|x-x^0\|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal Newton-Model Path and Initial Residual Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes a unique maximal path for a fixed nonsingular Newton model and a local linear residual reduction estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $G:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n$ be Lipschitz continuous on an open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. Suppose $G$ admits a nonsingular Newton approximation at $x\in\Omega$ and $G(x)\neq0$. For every $A(x,\cdot)\in\mathcal A(x)$, there is a unique Lipschitz path $p:I\to\Omega$ with maximal domain, where either $I=[0,1]$ or $I=[0,\bar\tau)$ for some $\bar\tau\in(0,1]$, such that $p(0)=x$, $G(x)+A(x,p(\tau)-x)=(1-\tau)G(x)$ for all $\tau\in I$, and $G(x)+A(x,\cdot-x)$ is a local homeomorphism near every point of the path. Moreover, for every $\gamma\in(0,1)$ there exists $\tau'>0$ with $\tau'\in I$ such that $\|G(p(\tau))\|\leq(1-\gamma\tau)\|G(x)\|$ for all $\tau\in[0,\tau']$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each selected nonsingular Newton model determines a unique maximal Lipschitz path that linearly scales the model residual. Along a sufficiently short initial segment, the true residual decreases at any prescribed fractional linear rate below one.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is open},\quad G:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n\text{ is Lipschitz continuous}
G\text{ admits a nonsingular Newton approximation at }x
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,p:I\to\Omega\text{ with the stated maximality and model-path properties, and }\forall\gamma\in(0,1)\ \exists\tau'>0:\ \|G(p(\tau))\|\leq(1-\gamma\tau)\|G(x)\|\ \forall\tau\in[0,\tau'].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Clarke implicit-function theorem with a Lipschitz solution branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local existence, uniqueness, and Lipschitz stability for a parameterized nonsmooth equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^n\) be Lipschitz continuous in a neighborhood of \((\bar x,\bar y)\), with \(G(\bar x,\bar y)=0\). Assume every matrix in \(\Pi_x\partial G(\bar x,\bar y)\) is nonsingular. Then there exist open neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(\bar y\) such that, for every \(y\in V\), the equation \(G(x,y)=0\) has a unique solution \(x=F(y)\in U\), where \(F(\bar y)=\bar x\), and \(F:V\to U\) is Lipschitz continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every projected generalized-Jacobian matrix for the x variables is nonsingular at a zero, the nearby equation has a unique local solution branch that depends Lipschitz-continuously on the parameter.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is Lipschitz continuous near }(\bar x,\bar y)
\forall H\in\Pi_x\partial G(\bar x,\bar y),\ H\text{ is nonsingular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni\bar x,\ V\ni\bar y\text{ open},\ \exists F:V\to U\text{ Lipschitz}:\ F(\bar y)=\bar x\ \land\ \forall y\in V,\ \{x\in U:G(x,y)=0\}=\{F(y)\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower Metric Bound Criterion for a Local Lipschitz Homeomorphism
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent characterization at a point of an open Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, \(x\in\mathcal D\), and \(\Phi:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n\). Then \(\Phi\) is a locally Lipschitz homeomorphism at \(x\) if and only if \(\Phi\) is locally Lipschitz continuous at \(x\) and there exist an open neighborhood \(\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal D\) of \(x\) and \(c>0\) such that \(\|\Phi(y)-\Phi(z)\|\ge c\|y-z\|\) for all \(y,z\in\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map is a locally Lipschitz homeomorphism at a point exactly when it is locally Lipschitz there and nearby distances satisfy a uniform positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi\text{ is a locally Lipschitz homeomorphism at }x\iff\left[\Phi\text{ is locally Lipschitz at }x\ \land\ \exists\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal D\text{ open with }x\in\mathcal N,\ \exists c>0,\ \forall y,z\in\mathcal N:\ \|\Phi(y)-\Phi(z)\|\ge c\|y-z\|\right]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Implicit Branch from an Auxiliary Lipschitz Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and quantitative Lipschitz stability of a local solution branch, with exhaustion of the localized solution set under the additional localization hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume that $W$ is a neighborhood of $0\in\mathbb{R}^k$ and that $\phi:W\to\mathbb{R}^k$ is single-valued and Lipschitz with modulus $\gamma$, with
\[
\phi(0)=z_0,\qquad \phi(\xi)\in\Sigma(\xi)\quad(\xi\in W).
\]
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there are neighborhoods $U_\varepsilon$ of $x_0$ and $V_\varepsilon$ of $z_0$ and a single-valued map $\sigma:U_\varepsilon\to V_\varepsilon$ such that
\[
\sigma(x_0)=z_0,\qquad \sigma(x)\in S(x)\quad(x\in U_\varepsilon),
\]
and $\sigma$ is Lipschitz with modulus $(\gamma+\varepsilon)L$, where $L$ is the constant from the contextual estimate (5.7). If, additionally, a neighborhood $V$ of $z_0$ satisfies
\[
\phi(\xi)=\Sigma(\xi)\cap V\quad(\xi\in W),
\]
then
\[
\sigma(x)=S(x)\cap V_\varepsilon\quad(x\in U_\varepsilon).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz selection of the auxiliary map through z0 induces, for every positive epsilon, a local Lipschitz solution branch through (x0,z0), with modulus (gamma+epsilon)L. If the selection is the entire localized auxiliary solution set, the branch is the entire localized original solution set.
assumptions_latex: \phi:W\to\mathbb{R}^k\text{ is single-valued and Lipschitz with modulus }\gamma
L\text{ is the constant from the contextual estimate (5.7)}
\text{For the strengthened conclusion: }\exists V\ni z_0\text{ such that }\phi(\xi)=\Sigma(\xi)\cap V\quad\forall\xi\in W
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U_\varepsilon\ni x_0,\ V_\varepsilon\ni z_0,\ \sigma:U_\varepsilon\to V_\varepsilon:\ \sigma(x_0)=z_0,\ \sigma(x)\in S(x),\ \operatorname{lip}(\sigma)\le (\gamma+\varepsilon)L;\quad [\phi(\xi)=\Sigma(\xi)\cap V]\Rightarrow[\sigma(x)=S(x)\cap V_\varepsilon]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mordukhovich Criterion for Set-Valued Lipschitz Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional coderivative characterization of the Aubin property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S:\mathbb R^p\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) have locally closed graph near \((\bar p,\bar x)\). Then \(S\) has the Aubin property at \((\bar p,\bar x)\) if and only if
\[
D^*S(\bar p,\bar x)(0)=\{0\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\operatorname{lip}S(\bar p,\bar x)=\lVert D^*S(\bar p,\bar x)\rVert^+,
\]
where the right side is the outer norm of the limiting coderivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued map is Lipschitz-like exactly when its coderivative sends zero only to zero, and the coderivative outer norm gives the exact modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(S:\mathbb R^p\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^n\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar p,\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\text{ is Aubin at }(\bar p,\bar x)\Longleftrightarrow D^*S(\bar p,\bar x)(0)=\{0\}\), and \(\operatorname{lip}S=\lVert D^*S\rVert^+\).

notation.meaning: Limiting coderivative of the solution map

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz Multifunction on a Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the global set-valued Lipschitz condition and its local-neighborhood version.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multifunction $F$ is Lipschitz on $C$ if $F(x)$ is defined and nonempty for every $x\in C$ and there is $K\ge 0$ such that, for all $x,y\in C$ and $v\in F(x)$, there exists $w\in F(y)$ with $\lVert v-w\rVert\le K\lVert x-y\rVert$. Equivalently, $F(x)\subset F(y)+K\lVert x-y\rVert B$ for all $x,y\in C$. It is Lipschitz near $\bar x$ if it is Lipschitz on some neighborhood of $\bar x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty-valued multifunction is Lipschitz on a set if each value at one point can be matched by a value at any other point with distance at most a fixed constant times the distance between the points. Equivalently, its values satisfy the corresponding ball-enlargement inclusion. Local Lipschitz continuity means this holds on a neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\ge0\ \forall x,y\in C:\ F(x)\subset F(y)+K\lVert x-y\rVert B

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz stability criterion for gradient-equation solution maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficiency, and under additional dependence, differentiability, and surjectivity assumptions necessity, of condition (4.81).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the finite-dimensional solution map (4.66), with \(\varphi\in\mathcal C^{1,1}\) around \(\bar w\), \(g\in\mathcal C^2\), and \(f\) Lipschitz continuous around \((\bar x,\bar y)\). Condition (4.81) is sufficient for \(S\) to be Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar y)\). Moreover, if \(g=g(y)\), \(\nabla g(\bar y)\) is surjective, and \(f\) is strictly differentiable at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) with surjective partial derivative \(\nabla_xf(\bar x,\bar y)\), then condition (4.81) is also necessary for this Lipschitz-like property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated finite-dimensional smoothness assumptions, condition (4.81) implies Lipschitz-like stability. It is also necessary when g depends only on y and the specified derivatives of g and f are surjective.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is Lipschitz continuous around }(\bar x,\bar y)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting-Normal Preimage Multiplier Rule
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A normal-cone representation under a nonsmooth constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E=\{u\in\mathbb R^n:\varphi(u)\in\Phi\}\), where \(\Phi\subset\mathbb R^k\) is closed, \(x\in E\), and \(\varphi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^k\) is Lipschitz near \(x\). Assume \(0\in\partial_L\langle v,\varphi\rangle(x)\) and \(v\in N^L_\Phi(\varphi(x))\) imply \(v=0\). Then every \(\zeta\in N^L_E(x)\) has a multiplier \(v\in N^L_\Phi(\varphi(x))\) satisfying \(\zeta\in\partial_L\langle v,\varphi\rangle(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated nonsmooth constraint qualification, every limiting normal to a Lipschitz constraint preimage is represented by a limiting normal multiplier for the target set and a limiting subgradient of the scalarized constraint map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\zeta\in N^L_E(x)\;\exists v\in N^L_\Phi(\varphi(x))\text{ such that }\zeta\in\partial_L\langle v,\varphi\rangle(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz-like property under composition with a single-valued inner mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition rule for a Lipschitz-like multifunction and a locally Lipschitz single-valued inner mapping, including a conditional modulus estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:X\to Y\) and \(F:Y\rightrightarrows Z\) be mappings between Asplund spaces, and let \(\bar z\in F(g(\bar x))\). Suppose that \(g\) is Lipschitz continuous around \(\bar x\), \(F\) has locally closed graph around \((g(\bar x),\bar z)\), and \(F\) is Lipschitz-like around that point. Then \(F\circ g\) is Lipschitz-like around \((\bar x,\bar z)\). If, additionally, \(\dim X<\infty\), \(F\) is coderivatively normal at \((g(\bar x),\bar z)\), and \(g\) is coderivatively normal at \(\bar x\), then \[\operatorname{lip}(F\circ g)(\bar x,\bar z)\leq \operatorname{lip}g(\bar x)\operatorname{lip}F(g(\bar x),\bar z).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composition with a locally Lipschitz single-valued inner mapping preserves the Lipschitz-like property. The product bound for the exact moduli additionally requires finite-dimensional X and coderivative normality of both mappings.
assumptions_latex: g\text{ is Lipschitz continuous around }\bar x
\operatorname{gph}F\text{ is locally closed around }(g(\bar x),\bar z)
F\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(g(\bar x),\bar z)
\dim X<\infty\text{ and the stated coderivative-normality assumptions hold for the modulus bound}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\circ g\text{ is Lipschitz-like around }(\bar x,\bar z);\quad \operatorname{lip}(F\circ g)(\bar x,\bar z)\leq\operatorname{lip}g(\bar x)\operatorname{lip}F(g(\bar x),\bar z)\text{ under the additional assumptions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coderivative Test for Canonical Lipschitz Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional limiting-coderivative criterion for metric regularity and Aubin stability of the canonical inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) have locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\). Then \(S=M^{-1}\) has the Aubin property at \((\bar y,\bar x)\), equivalently \(M\) is metrically regular at \((\bar x,\bar y)\), if and only if
\[
0\in D^*M(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y^*=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical Lipschitz stability holds exactly when no nonzero output covector has a coderivative image containing zero.
assumptions_latex: \(M:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) has locally closed graph near \((\bar x,\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^{-1}\) is Aubin at \((\bar y,\bar x)\) iff \([0\in D^*M(\bar x,\bar y)(y^*)\Rightarrow y^*=0]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coderivative Test for Canonical Lipschitz Stability

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Calmness of the canonical inverse corresponds to metric subregularity of the original mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=M^{-1}\text{ calm at }(\bar y,\bar x)\Longleftrightarrow M\text{ metrically subregular at }(\bar x,\bar y)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semiregular, regular, and strongly regular VI solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local solution stability of a fixed-set variational inequality under additive right-hand-side perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F). It is semiregular if, for every open neighborhood \mathcal N of x^* satisfying the standing localization condition (5.1.1), there exist c,\varepsilon>0 such that, for every q\in\mathbb R^n with \|q\|\le\varepsilon, \sup\{\|x-x^*\|:x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F+q)\cap\mathcal N\}\le c\|q\|. It is regular if, additionally, \operatorname{SOL}(K,F+q)\cap\mathcal N\ne\varnothing for every \|q\|\le\varepsilon. It is strongly regular if it is regular and, whenever \max\{\|q\|,\|q'\|\}\le\varepsilon, every x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F+q)\cap\mathcal N and x'\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F+q')\cap\mathcal N satisfy \|x-x'\|\le c\|q-q'\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Semiregularity gives a local linear displacement bound for all solutions under small additive perturbations. Regularity also guarantees that a nearby perturbed solution exists. Strong regularity further gives a uniform Lipschitz bound between solutions corresponding to two perturbation vectors.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal N\text{ is an open neighborhood of }x^*\text{ satisfying (5.1.1)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The displayed additive-perturbation bounds and local existence define semiregularity, regularity, and strong regularity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be reflexive. The stated weak lower-semicontinuity assumption is quantified over the empty ordinary-multiplier set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-Order Directional Expansion of the Optimal Value
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value expansion in a reflexive Banach space under directional regularity, a Lipschitz-scale near-optimal path, weak lower semicontinuity, and extended polyhedricity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X$ be reflexive. Assume: (i) $\Lambda(x_0,u_0)\neq\varnothing$ and directional regularity holds; (ii) $(P_{u(t)})$ has an $o(t^2)$-optimal solution $\bar x(t)$ with $\|\bar x(t)-x_0\|=O(t)$ for $t\geq0$; (iii) for every $\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0,u_0)$, the quadratic form $D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)(\cdot,\cdot)$ is weakly lower semicontinuous; and (iv) directional extended polyhedricity holds. Then $$\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(u(t))-v(u_0)-t\operatorname{val}(PL_d)}{\tfrac12t^2}=\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ}^R).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a reflexive Banach space, directional regularity, a near-optimal solution path remaining within order t of the reference solution, weak lower semicontinuity of all multiplier Hessian forms, and directional extended polyhedricity yield an exact second-order directional expansion of the value function. Its second-order coefficient is the value of the relaxed directional quadratic problem.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{v(u(t))-v(u_0)-t\operatorname{val}(PL_d)}{\tfrac12t^2}=\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ}^R)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hölder-scale optimizer and optimal-value expansion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak normalized-limit and value asymptotics, with conditional strong-limit and uniqueness refinements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X be a reflexive Banach space. Suppose that \Lambda(x_0,u_0)\neq\varnothing and directional regularity holds; the second-order sufficient conditions (3.136) hold at x_0\in\Phi(u_0); P_{u(t)} has an o(t)-optimal solution \bar x(t)\to x_0; D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0) is weakly lower semicontinuous for every \lambda\in\Lambda(x_0,u_0); and either 0\in\mathcal T_K^2(h) for every h\in C(x_0), or Robinson's constraint qualification and extended polyhedricity hold. Then \[\|\bar x(t)-x_0\|=O(t^{1/2}),\] every weak limit point of h(t):=t^{-1/2}(\bar x(t)-x_0) belongs to \mathcal S(\mathcal{DQ}^{2,R}), and \[v(u(t))=v(u_0)+\tfrac12t\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ}^{2,R})+o(t).\] If, additionally, every multiplier Hessian form is a Legendre form and the stated condition \xi_{\widetilde h}^{2,R}(\bar\lambda)=\operatorname{val}(DQ_{\widetilde h}^2) holds for a weak limit point, that point is a strong limit point and solves \mathcal{DQ}^{2,R}. If \mathcal{DQ}^{2,R} has the unique solution \widehat h, then every o(t)-optimal path \widehat x(t)\to x_0 satisfies \[\widehat x(t)=x_0+t^{1/2}\widehat h+o(t^{1/2}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated directional regularity, second-order, compactness, and geometric assumptions, nearly optimal solutions move on the square-root scale. Every weak normalized limit solves the relaxed dual quadratic problem, and the optimal value has the corresponding expansion. The additional Legendre-form and attainment assumptions give a strong limit point; uniqueness gives the full square-root expansion for every nearly optimal path.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a reflexive Banach space}
D_{xx}^2L(x_0,\lambda,u_0)\text{ is weakly lower semicontinuous for every }\lambda\in\Lambda(x_0,u_0)
\bigl[0\in\mathcal T_K^2(h)\ \forall h\in C(x_0)\bigr]\lor\bigl[\text{Robinson CQ and extended polyhedricity hold}\bigr]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\bar x(t)-x_0\|=O(t^{1/2}),\quad \operatorname{wLim}h(t)\subseteq\mathcal S(\mathcal{DQ}^{2,R}),\quad v(u(t))=v(u_0)+\tfrac12t\operatorname{val}(\mathcal{DQ}^{2,R})+o(t),\text{ with the stated conditional strong-limit and uniqueness refinements}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes weak first-order limits of approximate optimizer paths by the directional linearized problem and gives a converse realization result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose directional regularity holds at x_0\in\mathcal S(u_0) in direction d. knowledge_statements.title: Directionally Differentiable Solution Branches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional directional implicit-function result derived from exact tangent calculus and unique solvability of the linearized generalized equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P,X,Y\) be finite-dimensional normed spaces, let \(f:P\times X\to Y\), let \(Q:X\rightrightarrows Y\), and define \(S(p):=\{x\in X\mid0\in f(p,x)+Q(x)\}\). Suppose \(S\) has a single-valued Lipschitz localization \(s\) at \((\bar p,\bar x)\), \(f\) is continuously differentiable, \(Q\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,-f(\bar p,\bar x))\), and the graphical-derivative formula for \(S\) is exact there. If, for every \(h\in P\), the inclusion \[0\in\nabla_p f(\bar p,\bar x)h+\nabla_x f(\bar p,\bar x)k+DQ(\bar x,-f(\bar p,\bar x))(k)\] has a unique solution \(k=k(h)\), then \[s'(\bar p;h)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{s(\bar p+th)-s(\bar p)}{t}=k(h).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the exact graphical-derivative formula holds, unique solvability of every linearized directional generalized equation yields the directional derivative of the localized solution branch.
assumptions_latex: \(P,X,Y\) are finite-dimensional normed spaces, \(f:P\times X\to Y\), and \(Q:X\rightrightarrows Y\).
\(S(p):=\{x\in X\mid0\in f(p,x)+Q(x)\}\) has a single-valued Lipschitz localization \(s\) at \((\bar p,\bar x)\).
\(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(Q\) is proto-differentiable at \((\bar x,-f(\bar p,\bar x))\).
The graphical-derivative formula for \(S\) is exact at \((\bar p,\bar x)\).
For every \(h\in P\), the linearized generalized equation has a unique solution \(k(h)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s\) is directionally differentiable at \(\bar p\), and \(s'(\bar p;h)=k(h)\) for every \(h\in P\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hadamard Directional Differentiability of a Local Solution Branch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional differentiability notion for a single-valued localized solution selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local solution branch \(s:P\to X\) is Hadamard directionally differentiable at \(\bar p\) if, for every \(h\in P\), there exists \(s'(\bar p;h)\in X\) such that \[\lim_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\h'\to h}}\frac{s(\bar p+t h')-s(\bar p)}{t}=s'(\bar p;h).\] Its directional derivative is positively homogeneous: \(s'(\bar p;\alpha h)=\alpha s'(\bar p;h)\) for \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localized branch is Hadamard directionally differentiable when its first-order quotient has a stable limit under simultaneous perturbation of the step and direction.
assumptions_latex: \(P,X\) are normed spaces and \(s:P\to X\) is defined near \(\bar p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s'(\bar p;\alpha h)=\alpha s'(\bar p;h)\) for every \(\alpha>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global BIF Condition for Parametric VI Solution Branches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blanket condition imposed throughout the implicit-programming section, requiring a localized Lipschitz and directionally differentiable VI solution selection around every feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every $(\bar x,\bar y)\in\mathcal F$, there exist a neighborhood $V\times U$ of $(\bar x,\bar y)$ and a Lipschitz-continuous function $y:V\cap X\to U$ such that $y(\bar x)=\bar y$, $y$ is directionally differentiable at $\bar x$, and, for every $x\in V\cap X$, $y(x)$ is a solution in $U$ of the variational inequality $(F(x,\cdot),C(x))$. Thus, the implicit function $y$ is B-differentiable at $\bar x$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every feasible point, the condition postulates a local Lipschitz solution branch of the parameterized variational inequality that passes through that point and is directionally, and hence B-, differentiable at the base parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,V,U,y\text{ satisfying the stated localization, Lipschitz continuity, VI-solution, and directional-differentiability properties; in particular, }y\text{ is B-differentiable at }\bar x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hadamard directional derivative and first-order selection of minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric optimization under pointwise LICQ and inf-compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If LICQ holds at every x\in\mathcal S(u_0) and the problem is inf-compact, then v is Hadamard directionally differentiable at u_0 and
\[
v'(u_0;d)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal S(u_0)}D_uL(x,\lambda(x),u_0)d.
\]
Moreover, for u(t)=u_0+td+o(t), t\downarrow0, every limiting point of any path \bar x(t)\in\mathcal S(u(t)) belongs to
\[
\mathcal S_1(u_0,d)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal S(u_0)}D_uL(x,\lambda(x),u_0)d.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise LICQ and inf-compactness yield a Hadamard directional derivative of the optimal value, obtained by minimizing the parameter derivative of the Lagrangian over the unperturbed solution set. Limits of perturbed minimizers must attain this minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v'(u_0;d)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal S(u_0)}D_uL(x,\lambda(x),u_0)d,\quad \operatorname*{Limsup}_{t\downarrow0}\mathcal S(u(t))\subseteq\mathcal S_1(u_0,d)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional derivative of an infimum value function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric minimization under continuity, inf-compactness, and a directional sequential compatibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let v(u):=\inf_{x\in X}f(x,u), with solution set \mathcal S(u), and fix u_0. Suppose f is continuous on X\times U, the inf-compactness condition holds, each f_x(\cdot):=f(x,\cdot) is directionally differentiable at u_0 for x\in\Phi, and whenever d\in U, t_n\downarrow0, and x_n\in C, the sequence (x_n) has a limit point \bar x satisfying \limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{f(x_n,u_0+t_nd)-f(x_n,u_0)}{t_n}\ge f'_{\bar x}(u_0;d). Then v is directionally differentiable at u_0 and v'(u_0;d)=\inf_{x\in\mathcal S(u_0)}f'_x(u_0;d). Moreover, if x_n\in\mathcal S(u_0+t_nd) and t_n\downarrow0, every limit point \bar x of (x_n) lies in \mathcal S_1(u_0,d):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathcal S(u_0)}f'_x(u_0;d).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous inf-compact parametric minimization problem satisfying the stated directional sequential condition, the directional derivative of the optimal value is the infimum of the objective’s directional derivatives over the unperturbed solution set. Every limit point of optimizers along the perturbation direction minimizes those directional derivatives.
assumptions_latex: \forall x\in\Phi,\ f_x\text{ is directionally differentiable at }u_0
\forall d\in U,\ t_n\downarrow0,\ x_n\in C,\ \exists\bar x\in\operatorname{Limsup}x_n:\ \limsup_n\frac{f(x_n,u_0+t_nd)-f(x_n,u_0)}{t_n}\ge f'_{\bar x}(u_0;d)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hadamard sensitivity of an obstacle-control reduced objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directional derivative and strict-complementarity adjoint representation for a reduced obstacle-control objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F(u)=J_\tau(y(u),u), where y(u) solves the obstacle variational inequality. Then F is Hadamard directionally differentiable and, for every direction v, F'(u;v)=\int_\Omega (y(u)-\tau)z\,d\omega+N\int_\Omega uv\,d\omega, where z=y'(u;v). If strict complementarity holds at u, then F is Hadamard differentiable with derivative represented by p_u+Nu, where p_u\in C(u) is the unique solution of \int_\Omega\nabla p_u\cdot\nabla z'\,d\omega=\int_\Omega(y_u-\tau)z'\,d\omega for all z'\in C(u).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced objective formed from an obstacle state and its control is Hadamard directionally differentiable; its directional derivative combines the state directional derivative with the quadratic control term. Under strict complementarity it is fully Hadamard differentiable, and its derivative has an adjoint representation determined uniquely on the critical cone.
assumptions_latex: y(u)\text{ solves the obstacle variational inequality}
\text{for the second conclusion, strict complementarity holds at }u
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F'(u;v)=\int_\Omega(y(u)-\tau)z\,d\omega+N\int_\Omega uv\,d\omega,\ z=y'(u;v);\quad \text{under strict complementarity, }F'(u)=p_u+Nu\text{ with }p_u\in C(u)\text{ uniquely satisfying the stated variational equation}

where $K$ is the critical cone of $Q$ corresponding to $z_0$ and $-C(x_0,z_0)$.

Suppose that for every x\in X, f(x,\cdot) is G\hat ateaux differentiable, that f and D_uf are continuous on X\times U, and that the inf-compactness condition holds. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Second-Order Value Expansion and Directional Optimizer Derivative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sensitivity under directional second-order regularity and a Lipschitz near-optimal solution branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that $X$ is finite-dimensional, that $\Phi$ is second-order regular at $x_0$ in every direction $h\in C(x_0)$, and that there exists an $o(\|u-u_0\|^2)$-optimal solution $\bar x(u)$ of $(P_u)$ satisfying $\bar x(u)\to x_0$ and $\|\bar x(u)-x_0\|=O(\|u-u_0\|)$. Then $$\lim_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\ d'\to d}}\frac{v(u_0+td')-v(u_0)-tD_uf(x_0,u_0)d'}{\tfrac12t^2}=v(d),$$ where $v(d)$ is the optimal value of problem (4.351). If problem (4.351) has a unique optimal solution $\widehat h(d)$, then $\bar x$ is Hadamard directionally differentiable at $u_0$ in direction $d$ and $\bar x'(u_0;d)=\widehat h(d)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directional second-order regularity and a Lipschitz near-optimal branch give an exact second-order value expansion; uniqueness of the auxiliary optimizer then identifies the branch's Hadamard directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: \Phi\text{ is second-order regular at }x_0\text{ in every direction }h\in C(x_0)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{\substack{t\downarrow0\\ d'\to d}}\frac{v(u_0+td')-v(u_0)-tD_uf(x_0,u_0)d'}{\tfrac12t^2}=v(d),\quad\text{and if }\operatorname{argmin}(4.351)=\{\widehat h(d)\},\ \bar x'(u_0;d)=\widehat h(d)\text{ in the Hadamard sense}
